text: Why is a Layer 2 loop catastrophic where a Layer 3 loop is merely wasteful?
choices: An Ethernet frame has no hop count, so a looping frame circulates forever and every circuit multiplies it
explanation: The IP header has a TTL precisely so a routing loop kills a packet after a bounded number of hops. Ethernet, designed in 1980 for a single shared cable where loops were physically impossible, has no field to decrement. Within a second there are millions of copies and MAC tables thrash.
